title: Molecular biological analyses for phenotyping, biogeographic origin and identification
summary:
Analysis of short tandem repeats (STRs), based on PCR and capillary electrophoresis, is typically used to determine the source of a biological trace at a crime scene or for identification. To identify the origin of a biological trace, the analysed STR profile must be compared with a suspect or with a STR profile stored in a forensic DNA database. In some cases, however, there is no indication of identity or no comparative data is available in the corresponding reference databases. For these cases, so-called extended DNA analyses are required, which, among other things, enable an estimation of the physical appearance or biogeographical origin (BGA).
In addition to the classic method of capillary electrophoresis for molecular genetic analysis, so-called massive parallel sequencing (MPS) has become an increasingly used technique in routine applications. With the help of MPS, thousands of genetic markers for identification, parentage or phenotyping can be analysed simultaneously. This type of analysis thus enables a massive gain of information as well as an increase in efficiency on a technical level.
To conduct these investigations, we require buccal swabs. DNA is to be extracted from these and used to conduct a molecular biological analysis of various DNA markers. Methods for phenotyping, biogeographic origin and identification are to be established at the Institute of Legal Medicine in Frankfurt am Main. These include molecular genetic analyses of:

(1) eye, skin and hair colour of a person. The estimation of eye, skin and hair colour is based on the analysis of 41 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) on different genes that ultimately influence pigmentation. The detection of genotypes allows conclusions to be drawn about the visible phenotype.

(2) the biogeographical origin of a person. This can be estimated on the basis of population-specific SNPs, as well as the Y-chromosomal and mitochondrial haplotype.

(3) identification markers. There are certain DNA markers (SNPs and STRs) that are suitable for individualising a person because they have a high discriminatory power.

The aim of the study is to develop panels for the analysis of eye, skin and hair colour, BGA markers (mitochondrial DNA, Y-STRs and SNPs) and ID SNPs/STRs using minisequencing/capillary electrophoresis and massive parallel sequencing (MPS). These panels may eventually be combined, after modification, in a single MPS analysis to obtain a maximum amount of information with a single reaction.
conditions: It is not an illness, but a molecular genetic examination of a person's physical appearance, their biogeographic ancestry and their genetic fingerprint.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Test subjects are over 18 and can provide information about their externally visible characteristics and their biogeographical origin.
Exclusion criteria:
Test subjects are under 18 and cannot provide any information about their externally visible characteristics and biogeographical origin.
